DrWrinch: Fully Specified Bayes Factors for Process Tracing

Source: R/DrWrinch-package.R
DrWrinch-package.Rd

A researcher has coded the evidence into two counts: observations supporting the working theory and observations supporting a single rival. One model underlies everything this package computes. Each observation supports the working theory with probability \(\theta\), the share of the evidence that supports it. The working theory claims \(\theta > 1/2\) and the rival claims \(\theta \le 1/2\).

Details

Each claim is a range of shares rather than one share, so neither gives a probability for the counts on its own. The package computes the two Bayes factors of Lopez, Bowers, and Gajardo Cooper (2026). They share a numerator, the probability of the counts averaged over the shares above one half under uniform weights, and differ in the denominator. bf_uniform_weights() averages over the rival's shares under the same uniform weights. bf_worst_case() evaluates the rival at its most favorable share, one half when the counts favor the working theory, which makes its value the smallest any weights on the rival's shares can give. The paper's rule sets the rival aside, at least provisionally, when the first is 20 or more and the second is above 1.

bf_rescaled() computes the uniform-weights Bayes factor under other weights on the shares, and bf_worst_case() takes the same weights on the working theory's side. bf_uniform_weights_finite() and bf_worst_case_finite() compute both Bayes factors for documents read without replacement from an archive of known size. sens_bias() and sens_coding() report how biased the search, or how many observations re-coded, it would take before a researcher following the rule would no longer set the rival aside.

The package is named after Dorothy Maud Wrinch (1894–1976), whose joint papers with Harold Jeffreys (1919, 1921, 1923) developed the framework that became Jeffreys's theory of Bayes factors. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Maud_Wrinch.
